newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates higher amid strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates higher amid strong demand.

text.p: Some Croatian interbank rates rose in Wednesday morning's trade amid a stronger demand for kuna, dealers said.
Fresh trade totalled 26 million kuna, of which roughly one third was call money granted at a steady 11 percent.
But dealers said the one-month rate rose to 17 from 16 percent previously. The rate for one smaller one-week interbank loan also rose one percentage point to 13 percent.
The two-week rate was unchanged at 14 percent after rising from 13 percent two days ago.
A meagre 4.9 million kuna were settled in Tuesday's overnight trade as only two banks had shortfalls. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
